newsitem.title: FRANCE: French old-crop wheat rises on short covering.
newsitem.headline: French old-crop wheat rises on short covering.

text.p: Light short covering pushed old-crop wheat prices in Rouen higher on Monday but volume traded remained thin, dealers said.

Demand from Northern Europe remained weak though dealers said French wheat may benefit from a lower franc against the deutschemark parity after an unexpected strong showing by left parties in the first round of the parliamentary elections.
Rouen wheat was paid at 840 francs per tonne, excluding carry, for May delivery and at 835 francs for June delivery, both up five francs on Friday.
But September-December wheat into Rouen was steady at 880 francs per tonne.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
